content:
Road works insurance should follow the actual work sections, stages and parties, not only the contract total. Works under construction, contractor machinery, nearby property and third-party claims need separate questions. A performance guarantee is not a substitute for insurance against physical damage. Review the different purpose and documents of a performance guarantee separately.

Editorial revision: 26 November 2026. Planning material for 2027; the scenarios below are hypothetical, not incident or demand forecasts.

Who needs this review?

Main contractors, subcontractors and project owners in Moldova should compare the insurance obligations in their agreements with the proposed insurance documents. A requirement written in a works contract is not automatically incorporated into a policy. Procurement and legal requirements need their own specialist review.

Describe rehabilitation separately from new construction. Identify pavements, drainage, culverts, temporary works, material storage and machinery. If the scope includes bridge or tunnel work, use a separate structure and project-stage assessment. Record whether traffic, pedestrians or adjoining businesses remain near the work and which party manages the relevant project arrangements.

Risks, limitations and exclusions

Ask how the proposal treats accidental damage to works, fire, weather-related damage and relevant third-party claims. Do not translate the label all risks into protection for every mistake or expenditure. The accepted property, event definitions and list of insured parties must be read together.

Request clarification of defective work, the cost of correcting the defect itself, existing damage, wear of machinery, underground services and penalties for delay. These questions do not establish identical exclusions across policies. Distinguish an insured physical loss from contractual dissatisfaction or an unfulfilled performance promise.

Projects extending into 2027

Build a section-by-section calendar covering planned winter pauses, resumed work and staged acceptance. This is planning, not a forecast that a particular season will cause damage. A longer construction contract does not automatically extend an insurance period.

Consider a hypothetical additional culvert approved after the original estimate. Update the work description, methods, nearby property and schedule, not just the monetary total. Ask for written confirmation of the insurance treatment before treating a project amendment as accepted cover.

Prevention during pauses and changes

Use the project's competent technical team to review exposed stages, drainage arrangements and interfaces with continuing traffic before a planned pause. Keep the applicable site documents and unresolved recommendations current. This article provides no traffic-management or engineering instructions and does not substitute insurance for safe project execution.

What determines the price?

There is no verified universal 2027 rate for road projects in this guide. Assessment needs the work type, location, values, duration, construction methods, participants, claims history and requested limits. Separate works values from hired or owned plant and transported materials.

The premium is the price paid for insurance. A deductible is the insured's retained share of a loss under the contract. Compare proposals for the same sections and dates; a cheaper amount may describe a narrower period or omit existing property. Ask whether debris removal, professional fees or emergency expenses are included and subject to limits. (BNM: contract terms, checked 25 November 2026; general guidance, not individual policy conditions.)

A useful assessment file

Prepare the contract and relevant insurance clauses, bill of quantities, programme, site-organization documents and list of contractors. Add known utilities and existing structures through appropriate technical records. Share sensitive plans only through agreed channels.

At an incident, prioritize safety and competent intervention. Preserve the section reference, stage, observations and relevant costs where safe. Follow the contract's notification procedure. An invoice establishes expenditure, not by itself entitlement to indemnity.

Three situations: what to compare before deciding

The MOLDASIG construction and installation page, checked on 26 November 2026, lists roads among works objects. This is not acceptance of all road assets, machinery, liability or operating-period damage.

  • Works, materials and contractor plant share a site: compare ownership and valuation for each. Prepare the schedule of works, materials and equipment. Check accepted objects rather than treating the full contract price as a complete inventory.
  • Work is near a third-party utility: compare the scope, available surveys and responsibilities without publishing sensitive plans. Prepare relevant contract records. Request actual liability conditions; a works entry does not establish payment of every third-party claim.
  • Seasonal pause, restart or partial opening in 2027: compare the actual programme with the declared period and stage. Keep dated changes and handover records. Verify any amendment before relying on the original construction description.

Frequently asked questions

What factors determine the road-works premium?

Present the work type, sections, values, methods, duration, participants and requested limits. Separate machinery, existing property and transported materials. Compare identical scope and dates, including planned pauses or partial openings. A lower amount may reflect a shorter period or omitted object rather than the same protection at a better price.

Which project records help an initial assessment?

Prepare the relevant contract clauses, estimate, programme, site-organization documents and participant list. Add available technical records for existing structures and utilities. Identify revisions by section and date so the proposal can be compared with the actual works. Missing information should remain an open point, not an assumption of acceptance.

What should we record after damage on a work section?

First follow safety and competent project intervention. Where safe, retain the section reference, work stage, observed conditions, findings and relevant costs, distinguishing urgent actions from reinstatement. Notify under the policy procedure and ask about inspection and evidence. Neither a contractor statement nor a repair invoice alone proves insurer acceptance.

What happens when part of the road opens before the project ends?

Ask how partial acceptance, public use and the transition to operation affect the actual policy. Keep section-level dates and confirmations rather than assigning the entire road one status. A construction-contract extension or internal opening decision is not automatically an amendment to the insured period or stage.

Are underground services and delay penalties included in general liability?

Describe known utilities and request the applicable conditions for third-party damage. Keep delay penalties, physical loss and any separate completion consequences distinct. A liability heading does not establish inclusion of every contractual promise, and a clause in the works contract is not automatically reproduced in the insurance contract.

Discuss the project with ING Broker. The broker organizes insurance enquiries and explains options; the insurer decides acceptance, conditions and claims. This guide confirms no automatic product availability or project-specific coverage.
